name: ID-02
label: Safe R

key_factors: Strong Republican district (R+13 PVI) with long-serving incumbent Mike Simpson
Simpson's large fundraising edge ($1.1M raised vs ~$107K for Gilbreath)
Prediction markets price Democratic chances at about 4%
No public polling; fundamentals and money dominate the picture
model.rationale: Simpson is a well-funded incumbent in a district that leans Republican by double digits, and markets give the challenger only a token chance. With no polls or expert ratings suggesting otherwise, the race sits firmly in Safe R territory.
model.watch: A major late outside-spending intervention or an unexpected scandal could narrow the margin, though not plausibly the outcome.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Idaho's 2nd District is a solidly Republican seat, and Mike Simpson has held it for decades. He enters the general election with a large financial advantage, having raised over $1.1 million to challenger Ellie Gilbreath's roughly $107,000, and with the benefit of incumbency in a district that favored Republicans by about 13 points at the presidential level.

Gilbreath faces long odds with minimal resources and no outside spending on either side. Prediction markets give her roughly a 4% chance of an upset, and the absence of any public polling reflects how little competitive attention this race has drawn. The expected outcome is a comfortable Simpson win in the mid-to-high teens.
